seen.where: ANOM page images by IIIF, 22 Nov 2026: COL C8 A 51 f. 109 (record ark:/61561/zn401hgefcg, images FRANOM23_C8A_051_0204-0214), C8 A 58 f. 33 (ark:/61561/zn401uptqh, images FRANOM23_C8A_058_0059-0066), C8 A 59 f. 158 (ark:/61561/zn401rsnkma, images FRANOM23_C8A_059_0268-0279); the three pieces the block of 3 Nov 2026 had not viewed, each with its neighbouring leaves.
seen.extent: C8 A 51 ff. 109-113 (Champigny, Fort-Royal, 21 Dec 1740, duplicate): f. 109r clear, then about 100-110 lines of numbers to f. 113r with clear passages between. C8 A 58 ff. 33-34 (Caylus, Martinique, 10 Mar 1748, duplicate): about 90 lines of numbers, the letter in code apart from the address and close. C8 A 59 ff. 158-161 (Bompar and Hurson, Fort-Royal, 14 Nov 1751, duplicate): clear opening, then about 140 lines of numbers to f. 161r. Line counts by eye from contact sheets (within about 10%); one page of each checked line by line at full size.
seen.cipher: Number code in groups of up to three digits. Every piece carries the ministry's contemporary decipherment: C8 A 51 f. 109 and C8 A 59 f. 158 have French written above each line (all 20 lines of f. 110r and all 24 of f. 159v checked); C8 A 58 f. 33 has it in a narrow column in the left margin, continued below the signature on f. 34r and onto f. 34v, ending 'avec toute la promptitude possible. J'ai l'honneur d'être &c.'

1204.closed: Read at the time, as far as seen. All three pieces the block of 3 Nov 2026 had not viewed carry the ministry's contemporary decipherment: C8 A 51 f. 109 (Champigny, 21 Dec 1740) and C8 A 59 f. 158 (Bompar and Hurson, 14 Nov 1751) between the lines, C8 A 58 f. 33 (Caylus, 10 Mar 1748) in the margin and after the signature. With ff. 13, 79, 323 and C8 A 51 f. 116 seen on 3 Nov, ff. 40, 44, 54-56v, 59, 63, 67 attested by targets/champigny1744, and f. 57 read there, every piece the lead names is read at the time or since, except C8 A 56 ff. 73, 85 and 253, which no one has yet recorded looking at. If those three are glossed too, the lead can be closed as read.
1204.supersedes: Same verdict as the block of 3 Nov 2026, with new evidence: the three pieces it listed as not viewed (C8 A 51 f. 109, C8 A 58 f. 33, C8 A 59 f. 158) have now been seen and all are deciphered on the leaf. The calendar's 'part not decrypted' for C8 A 56 f. 54 is its enclosure f. 57, read in targets/champigny1744. Also: f. 109 is of 1740 and f. 158 of 1751, outside King George's War; only C8 A 58 f. 33 (March 1748) falls in it.

2730.unvetted: Not digitised: BnF fr. 3329, fr. 3409 and fr. 4717 have no Gallica copy (catalogue records ark:/12148/cc497913, cc49879s, cc57767r show none, and Gallica's search for 'Français 3329' and its manuscript search for Humières with 'chiffre' find printed books and other volumes only, 22 Nov 2026); the leaves need a BnF reproduction order or the Richelieu reading room. Corrections from the BnF record of fr. 3329, read 22 Nov 2026, which agree with research/audit_2026-11-16_omont_shelfmarks: no. 81 (Maineville, Chenonceaux, 7 May 1577) is f. 164 and no. 82 (Pierre de Roncherolles, Pont-Saint-Pierre, 9 May 1577) f. 165, not ff. 104-105; no. 107 (Maineville, 'D'Ennet', 30 Sept, 'Avec chiffre', f. 197) is missing from the lead; no. 1 is a 'Table de déchiffrement anonyme' and no. 2 a 'Table de chiffrement de Monsieur de Humières pour correspondre avec Monsieur d'Entragues', so they are not a matched pair and no. 2 need not be the key of these letters; the governor of Péronne is named in the same volume as 'J[acques de] Humyeres' (no. 84, f. 168, 18 May 1577), not Jean, and the record does not call him marquis. The audit also notes fr. 3409 no. 39 ('Chiffre') and fr. 4717 no. 11 ('Clef d'un chiffre') as keys in the other two volumes.
